ai.description: The Reticulated Python is the world's longest snake, reaching over 6 meters. It features a complex, diamond-shaped dorsal pattern of black, yellow, and brown, with a distinct dark line on the head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Reticulated Python is best distinguished by its complex, diamond-shaped dorsal pattern and a thin, dark line running precisely down the center of its head.
ai.habitat: The reticulated python inhabits tropical rainforests, woodlands, and mangrove swamps, typically ranging from sea level to elevations of approximately 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The reticulated python is primarily nocturnal, using its heat-sensing labial pits to ambush prey in the dark before constricting it with immense muscular force.
ai.reproductionNotes: The reticulated python is oviparous, laying clutches of 15–80 eggs. In India, breeding typically occurs during the cooler months, with hatching after 80–90 days.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Malayopython reticulatus* is restricted to the Nicobar Islands, occurring from sea level up to moderate elevations in tropical forests.
